title: Enzymatic PET depolymerization: a review of engineering biocatalysts and systems for efficient plastic deconstruction.
abstract: The ever-increasing accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste poses a severe threat to global ecosystems and human health. Biological upcycling (integrating enzymatic depolymerization with microbial conversion of the resulting monomers) has emerged as a promising approach to overcome the limitations of traditional mechanical and chemical recycling. This review provides a systematic and critical synthesis of recent advances in PET bio-upcycling, covering the period from 2016 to 2026. We first discuss the discovery, classification, structural features, and catalytic mechanisms of PET-hydrolyzing enzymes, highlighting the rate-limiting constraints imposed by glass transition temperature, substrate crystallinity, interfacial interactions, and product inhibition. We then evaluate protein engineering strategies that have dramatically enhanced thermostability, substrate binding, and multi-enzyme synergy, yielding benchmark variants capable of near-complete depolymerization of post-consumer PET within hours to days. Concurrent innovations in whole-cell biocatalysis, enzyme immobilization, surface display, and microbial consortia are examined, with emphasis on how metabolic division of labor and substrate channeling can alleviate product inhibition and process mixed plastic waste. We also summarize metabolic engineering efforts that have enabled conversion of PET-derived terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG) into more than 25 value-added products, including biopolymers, platform chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and specialty compounds. Finally, we discuss remaining technological barriers, economic feasibility, and future frontiers (including computational enzyme design, synthetic consortia, tandem chemo-biological processes, and industrial-scale demonstration) and propose a phased roadmap for industrial translation. This review aims to provide a comprehensive resource for advancing PET bio-upcycling from laboratory innovation toward practical implementation in a circular plastics economy.

title: Electrospun Co3O4/CeO2 hollow nanotubes for photocatalytic degradation of PET plastics with peroxymonosulfate activation: Performance and DFT insight.
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics cause significant environmental harm. Traditional treatment methods, such as landfilling and incineration, can cause secondary pollution. Here, an efficient synergistic photocatalytic system is presented, based on Co3O4/CeO2 hollow nanotubes prepared by electrospinning, to activate peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and promote the degradation of PET plastics. The results show that the as-prepared Co3O4/CeO2 composite catalyst exhibits the best performance under illumination; the weight loss rate of PET can reach ∼82.7 ± 4.5% in the presence of a 3 mM PMS solution (pH 7). The effects of parameters (e.g., PMS dose and coexisting anions) on PET degradation were systematically investigated. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and free radical quenching experiments confirm that the •OH, 1O2, and SO4•- active species contribute the most to the degradation of PET plastics. Density Functional Theory analysis shows that Co-d-pDOS and Ce-f-pDOS modulations in Co3O4/CeO2 synergistically enhance the PET photocatalytic decomposition efficiency. Finally, we discuss the mechanism by which the catalyst/light/PMS system degrades PET in water.

title: Depolymerization of PET and Polyamide 66 Wastes Using an Iron(III) Recoverable Lewis-Brønsted Aqueous System.
abstract: The accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyamide 66 (PA66) in municipal and industrial waste streams represents a major challenge to global sustainability efforts. In this work, we report the development and optimization of a low-cost, iron-recoverable, and reconstitutable Lewis-Brønsted aqueous solution (LBAS) system for the selective depolymerization of post-consumer PET and PA66 wastes. The method employs a recyclable reaction medium and operates under mild conditions (150 °C, 2 h), achieving high monomer yields with excellent selectivity. The resulting terephthalic acid, adipic acid, and hexamethylenediammonium chloride were efficiently recovered and purified using straightforward separation techniques, whereas ethylene glycol was recovered as a stream suitable for purification by conventional industrial methods. A proof-of-concept experiment confirmed that PET and PA66 can also be depolymerized in the same medium, even though cross reactions between adipic acid and ethylene glycol prevent the quantitative monomer recovery. Therefore, mixed PET/PA66 feeds require prior separation to recover the individual monomers effectively. Overall, results demonstrate a scalable and environmentally benign approach for the chemical recycling of PET and PA66, contributing to a more sustainable plastic lifecycle and circular materials economy.

title: Detection, characterization, and quantification of microplastics in human biological matrices: a systematic review.
mesh: Female; Humans; Environmental Monitoring; Microplastics; Male
abstract: The presence of microplastics (MPs) in the environment represents an emerging risk to human health, with growing evidence of detection in human biological matrices. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on the detection, quantification, and characterization of MPs in human biological matrices. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus databases. Original research articles published in English up to 2025 that involved human participants were included, specifically selecting observational studies. The 40 included studies confirmed MPs in multiple human biological matrices, including blood, urine, feces, placenta, breast milk, semen, lung, and heart tissue. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) was used to assess the quality and risk of bias of the individual studies. Substantial methodological heterogeneity was observed in analytical techniques, including Fourier-transform infrared microspectroscopy (μFTIR), micro-Raman spectroscopy (μ-Raman), laser direct infrared spectroscopy (LDIR), and pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS), as well as in the reporting units and limits of detection. Most studies reported fragments and fibers, with a predominance of polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), polystyrene (PS), and polyethylene terephthalate (PET). NOS assessment showed that 52.5% of studies were of moderate quality, indicating that while the frequent detection of these particles suggests widespread human contact, significant methodological shortcomings and potential analytical overestimations limit the accurate quantification of systemic exposure and the strength of causal inferences. The widespread detection of MPs raises public health concerns regarding chronic exposure and potential health implications. However, current evidence remains insufficient to establish causal relationships, underscoring the urgent need for rigorous epidemiological studies.

title: Chemical Degradation of Waste Polyethylene Terephthalate and Its Application in Developing Asphalt Additives.
abstract: To address the low resource-recovery efficiency of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and the shortage of high-performance eco-friendly asphalt modifiers, PET-derived functional additives were fabricated in this work via zinc-acetate-catalyzed alcoholysis of waste PET followed by repolymerization of the obtained degradation fragments. Owing to the diverse origins of waste PET feedstock, noticeable fluctuations in molecular-weight parameters are commonly encountered. Nevertheless, waste PET can be effectively depolymerized into relatively low-molecular-weight derivatives under the proposed catalytic alcoholysis conditions. This study systematically investigated the effects of different PET degradation pathways on the molecular architecture, molecular-weight distribution, and thermal stability of as-prepared PET-derived asphalt additives. It further uncovers the intrinsic structure-performance relationships between molecular characteristics and critical asphalt properties, including rheological behavior, interfacial adhesion, high-temperature rutting resistance, and low-temperature elastic recovery. Homogeneous alcoholysis conducted at 220 °C enables efficient depolymerization of waste PET to yield derivatives with tailorable molecular weights. The resultant amphiphilic alcoholysis products can reduce asphalt viscosity and ameliorate water stability, rendering them promising warm-mix anti-stripping additives. By contrast, repolymerized PET derivatives are capable of constructing cross-linked networks within asphalt matrix, which substantially boost the high-temperature modulus and fatigue resistance of modified asphalt. Distinct from conventional physical blending approaches that are plagued by inferior interfacial compatibility and marginal performance improvement, this chemical modification strategy affords PET-based additives with tunable functions for different engineering scenarios. These findings provide technical support for high-value recycling of waste PET and the development of sustainable low-carbon asphalt materials.

title: Molecular-Level Structure Regulation via Sequential Pre-Crosslinking and Friedel-Crafts Hypercrosslinking: Fabrication of Bimetallic Doped Porous Carbon Electrocatalysts.
abstract: Owing to high surface inertness and insufficient active sites, traditional carbons cannot anchor and disperse metal species evenly, restricting catalytic activity. Via polymer precursor design, the components, functional groups and pore architecture can be tailored molecularly and preserved upon carbonization, thus regulating carbon microstructure, surface properties and active centers efficiently. This work focuses on the synthesis and structural tuning of polystyrene-based precursors using a three-step procedure of pre-crosslinking, Friedel-Crafts hypercrosslinking, and activation. The materials possess abundant mesopores ranging from 7 to 30 nm, which serve as an ideal platform for the efficient anchoring of metal ions and mass transfer during the subsequent carbonization and functionalization processes. Based on the strong adsorption and exchange ability of sulfonic acid groups, transition metal ions such as Co, Ni and Fe were uniformly doped on the surface of nanoparticles and carbonized at 300-600 °C in an air atmosphere to realize the conversion of the polymer skeleton to a carbon matrix and the in situ formation of metal species into oxide nanoparticles. At the application performance level, the prepared Co/Ni bimetallic-carbon-doped material exhibits excellent electrocatalytic activity in the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction. The overpotential is only 0.3478 V at a current density of 10 mA cm-2. After 50 cycles of cyclic voltammetry, the voltage fluctuation is only 0.026 V.

title: Effects of Storage Temperature and Packaging Type on the Postharvest Quality of Finger Lime (Citrus australasica).
abstract: Finger lime (Citrus australasica F.Muell.) is a native Australian citrus species with increasing commercial value because of its unique sensory, visual and nutritional properties. However, like other citrus species, it is highly perishable and susceptible to postharvest quality deterioration. Despite its growing importance, limited research has examined how commercial packaging and storage temperature affect its quality. Therefore, this study investigated the combined effects of three commonly used types of packaging (net bags, recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) punnets and moulded cardboard clamshells) and three storage temperatures (room temperature (RT; ~25 °C), 8 °C and 4 °C) on finger lime quality over eight weeks. The quality parameters examined included weight loss, firmness, colour, visual appearance and overall marketability, as well as nutritional properties, including total phenolic content, total flavonoid content and antioxidant capacity. Packaging and temperature both significantly affected fruit marketability. Fruit stored at RT quickly lost quality in all packaging types. Fruit stored at 4 °C retained firmness, colour, total phenolic content, flavonoid content and antioxidant capacity better than fruit stored at 25 °C or 8 °C; however, chilling injury and fungal growth developed at 4 °C, with approximately 20% of the fruit in each packaging treatment deemed unsaleable by Week 8. At 8 °C, no chilling injury, visible fungal growth or shrivelling was observed. Although approximately 60% of fruit in cardboard clamshells and net bags were classified as unsaleable because of loss of freshness, approximately 80% of fruit in punnets remained saleable until the end of the trial. Overall, storage at 8 °C in rPET punnets provided the best balance between quality retention and marketability among the combinations of packaging type and storage temperature examined in this study.

title: Recycled PET/Sepiolite Composite Adsorbent for Methylene Blue Removal: Formulation, RSM Optimisation, Reusability, and Adsorption Mechanism.
mesh: Methylene Blue; Adsorption; Magnesium Silicates; Polyethylene Terephthalates; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Hydrogen-Ion Concentration; Temperature; Water Purification; Kinetics; Recycling
abstract: This study explores the valorisation of post-industrial recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) via incorporation of sepiolite clay to develop a composite adsorbent for methylene blue (MB) dye removal. The composite formulation was evaluated by varying the rPET concentration, TFA:DCM solvent ratio, sepiolite content, and blending time. The selected formulation had an average particle size of 267.10 nm, a specific surface area of 0.67 m2/g, and a pore volume of 0.003925 cm3/g. Adsorption conditions were then optimised using a five-factor, three-level Box-Behnken design, considering contact time, MB concentration, adsorbent dosage, pH, and temperature. The resulting quadratic model was statistically significant (F = 114.18, p < 0.0001), with R2 = 0.9892, adjusted R2 = 0.9805, and predicted R2 = 0.9568; however, the lack-of-fit was also significant (F = 90.90, p < 0.0001), indicating that model predictions should be interpreted within the investigated factor ranges. At the selected conditions of 62.5 min, 25.5 mg/L MB, 2.55 g/50 mL adsorbent, pH 7, and 55 °C, the model predicted an MB removal efficiency of 99.03%. The adsorbent retained at least 93% reusability efficiency after six adsorption-washing-reuse cycles. The kinetic data were described more closely by the pseudo-second-order model, whereas the Freundlich model provided a better representation of the equilibrium data (R2 = 0.9976). Thermodynamic results indicated that adsorption was favourable and exothermic within the investigated temperature range. Overall, the results show that post-industrial PET can be converted into a value-added sepiolite-containing adsorbent for MB removal.

title: In-Situ Catalytic Pyrolysis of Polystyrene with Sewage Sludge-Derived Catalysts: Sewage Sludge Ash, Sewage Sludge Char, and Fe-Impregnated Acid-Leached Sewage Sludge Char.
abstract: Sewage sludge (SS)-derived materials were investigated as low-cost heterogeneous catalytic materials for polystyrene (PS) pyrolysis, focusing on the effects of thermal treatment, HCl leaching, and Fe impregnation. Sewage sludge ash (SSA), sewage sludge char (SSC), and HCl-leached Fe-impregnated sewage sludge char (Fe-LSSC) were evaluated as in-situ catalytic materials. Catalyst-to-PS ratios of 1:1-1:10 were investigated in a horizontal semi-batch tubular reactor operated in an in-situ catalyst-polymer contact mode at 800 °C. Thermal pyrolysis produced 63.9 wt.% PyOil and 12.6 wt.% PyGas. SSA increased the PyOil yield to 78.0 wt.% at 1:10 and promoted lighter aromatics; at 1:1, light aromatics increased to 66.8 wt.%, BTEX from 5.8 to 24.58 wt.%, and PAHs decreased to 11.8 wt.%. SSC showed a weaker, non-monotonic effect, with PyOil decreasing to 54.4 wt.% and PyChar increasing to 4.7 wt.% at 1:2. Fe-LSSC produced the strongest changes, increasing PyGas to 28.0 wt.% at 1:1 and H2 to 75.3 vol.% at 1:2. The gasoline-range fraction reached 82.1 wt.% at 1:2, while PAHs decreased to 8.79 wt.% at 1:1. Catalyst reuse altered gas composition, whereas thermal regeneration partially restored catalytic behavior. Overall, SS-derived materials exhibited distinct, loading-dependent catalytic functions, while HCl leaching and Fe impregnation enhanced the conversion of PS pyrolysis vapors toward lighter aromatic and gaseous products.

title: Selective Upcycling of Waste PET into Di(2-ethylhexyl) Terephthalate via a Hybrid Organometallic Catalytic Strategy for PVC Plasticizer Applications.
abstract: The selective conversion of post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into value-added plasticizers offers a promising pathway for advancing polymer circularity within the scope of the circular economy approach. Herein, waste PET bottles were directly upcycled into di(2-ethylhexyl) terephthalate (DOTP) via degradative alcoholysis/transesterification with 2-ethylhexanol using four organometallic catalyst systems: butylstannic acid (F), monobutyltin tris(2-ethylhexanoate) (TK), titanium tetraisopropoxide (T), and a hybrid organotin-titanium system (TKT). PET conversion ranged from 84 to 94%, with the T catalyst affording the highest conversion (94%). Notably, the hybrid TKT catalyst provided the most favorable overall performance, achieving an 81% isolated yield and 85.4% selectivity. GC-FID analysis revealed that DOTP-TKT achieved a 92.0% chromatographic area, while GPC confirmed that this product had the lowest proportion of residual oligomers (15.13%) among all PET-derived samples. FTIR and 1H-NMR spectroscopy further confirmed efficient PET-to-DOTP transformation, with DOTP-TKT displaying the closest structural correspondence to commercial DOTP. Amongst the PET-derived products, DOTP-TKT exhibited the most favorable thermal behavior, with a principal maximum degradation temperature (Tmax) of approximately 283.5 °C. When incorporated into PVC, PET-derived DOTP-TKT showed enhanced tensile strength, elastic modulus, and elongation at break compared with commercial DOTP. These findings demonstrate that the combined Ti-Sn catalyst system simultaneously promotes selective PET depolymerization and product formation while limiting oligomeric residues, providing an effective route for converting post-consumer PET into functional, high-value PVC plasticizers within a circular polymer economy.

title: Juncus Acutus fiber-recycled expanded polystyrene composites for lower-impact insulation: experimental characterization and numerical thermal analysis.
abstract: In response to the growing demand for lower-impact building insulation materials, this study investigates composites combining Juncus Acutus (JA) fibers with recycled expanded polystyrene (EPS) as a strategy for valorizing biomass and polymeric waste. Three JA/EPS formulations (70/30, 60/40, and 50/50) were experimentally characterized in terms of density, thermal properties, and compressive strength, followed by life-cycle assessment and transient numerical analysis. Increasing the JA content from 50 to 70% reduced the bulk density from 371.6 to 289.9 kg·m⁻3 and thermal conductivity from 0.117 to 0.096 W·m⁻1·K⁻1, while thermal diffusivity decreased by approximately 15% and specific heat capacity increased by about 10%. Despite the reduction in compressive strength with increasing fiber content, the JA70 formulation reached 0.16 MPa, indicating adequate mechanical integrity for handling and use in non-structural insulation applications. Among the investigated formulations, JA70 provided the most favorable balance between thermal and mechanical properties. Its cradle-to-gate global warming potential was estimated at 1.1 kg CO2-eq·kg⁻1, while transient numerical simulations demonstrated improved thermal inertia and indoor temperature regulation under representative climatic conditions. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of JA fiber-recycled EPS composites as promising lower-impact insulation materials, while also highlighting the need to further address solvent-related impacts, moisture resistance, fire performance, and long-term durability before practical building application.

title: Upcycling Recycled PET into High-Performance Polyurethane Coating and Engineering Materials: Effect of NCO Index on Mechanical, Stability, and Surface Properties.
abstract: Upcycling of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste into high-value polymeric materials offers a promising pathway toward circular and sustainable polymer engineering. In this work, polyurethane (PU) films were synthesized from recycled PET (rPET)-based polyols, and the influence of the isocyanate index (NCO index: 100-200) on the network structure and functional properties of the resulting materials was investigated. FT-IR results supported the formation of urethane linkages between the rPET-based polyol and polymeric methylene diphenyl diisocyanate (PMDI), indicating successful network formation. Increasing the NCO index significantly enhanced cross-link density, reflected by an increase in gel content from 54.97 to 93.46% and a decrease in swelling ratio from 254.58% to 133.30%. This structural evolution led to improved mechanical performance, with tensile strength and Young's modulus reaching 7.26 and 5.29 N/mm2, respectively. Thermal analysis further revealed an increase in glass transition temperature (-32.05-0.93 °C) and enhanced thermal stability with higher char yields (17.57-24.71%). Surface analyses demonstrated smoother, denser, and more hydrophobic morphologies at elevated NCO indices. An optimal balance of mechanical, thermal, and surface properties was achieved at NCO indices of 150-175, highlighting the potential of rPET-based PU films as sustainable coating and engineering materials for advanced applications.

title: Microplastic pollution characteristics in global marine sediments: A meta-analysis.
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) pollution in marine environments has attracted widespread attention worldwide. Sediments are hotspots of MPs pollution. However, a comprehensive understanding of the distribution characteristics and driving factors of microplastics in coastal sediments is still lacking. The results revealed substantial variation in sediment MP abundance, with values ranging from 7.6 to 4213 particles/kg; the overall pooled abundance was 186.24 particles/kg (95% CI: 132.39-262.00), with substantial residual heterogeneity among the included estimates. Smaller MPs (<1 mm) accounted for over 60% of all detected MPs in global sediments. Transparent, fibrous and Polyethylene were the most common color, morphology and polymer type of MPs, respectively. Based on redundancy analysis (RDA), driving factors of MP morphological characteristics were explored. The results showed that flotation density and identification methods were the main sources of methodological bias in the observed MP characteristics. Significant differences in microplastic color distribution were observed among different countries. We divided the studies into four subgroups according to the distance from the coast. Although MP abundance exhibited certain spatial variations across regions, regional factors could explain only a small fraction of the observed heterogeneity. In contrast, the multivariable model explained 48.3% of the heterogeneity, highlighting the importance of methodological variability and the need for more standardized sampling and analytical procedures. This study identified small MPs and low-density polymers as key components of global sedimentary MP pollution and highlighted the need for standardized detection methods, supporting targeted monitoring of these MPs and harmonized protocols for global marine sediment assessment.

title: Evidence of microplastic ingestion in ringed seals (Pusa hispida) from the Canadian Arctic.
abstract: Ringed seals (Pusa hispida) play a crucial role in Arctic marine food webs, serving as predators of fish and invertebrates, and as prey for polar bears (Ursus maritimus). They are also a critical food source for Inuit subsistence. However, there is limited data on microplastic accumulation in Arctic pinnipeds, including ringed seals. To better understand the extent of ingestion and potential accumulation of microplastics in ringed seals from the Canadian Arctic, 30 ringed seal stomachs were collected in collaboration with Inuit Hunters from Arviat and Resolute Bay, Nunavut, Canada, in 2021. All suspected microplastics underwent analysis by Raman microspectroscopy to identify polymer type, and all identified microplastics were counted and categorized based on size, color and morphology. Microplastics were present in 23 out of 30 (77%) seal stomachs, with abundances ranging from 0 to 6 particles per seal (mean = 2.0 ± 1.6 pcs/seal). Fragments were the most prevalent morphology identified (55%), followed by fibers (42%) and films (3.3%). Most particles were unidentified anthropogenic particles and polyester fibers. Microplastic abundances were similar between sexes and between seals collected from the two locations, and no relationships were found between microplastic abundances and age or any morphometric measurements. This study provides new data confirming the presence and characteristics of microplastics ingested by ringed seals harvested in Arviat and Resolute Bay, Nunavut, Canada, and provides baseline information for future plastic pollution monitoring programs in the region.

title: Microplastics in commercially important marine fish from Giresun Province, Türkiye: A baseline assessment of tissue distribution, polymer composition, spatial patterns, and potential environmental and ecological risk.
abstract: This study investigated the occurrence, characteristics, and spatial distribution of microplastics in muscle tissues and guts of commercially important fish species with different feeding habits (Pomatomus saltatrix, Mullus barbatus, Trachurus trachurus, Engraulis encrasicolus, Mugil cephalus, Merlangius merlangus, and Sarda sarda) from Giresun coast of the Black Sea. Microplastic contamination and polymer-associated hazard characteristics were evaluated using the contamination factor (CF), pollution load index (PLI), polymer hazard index (PHI), and potential ecological risk index (PERI). Microplastics were detected in both muscle tissue and gut, with substantial variation among species and tissues. The highest microplastic abundance was observed in the muscle of P. saltatrix (41.3 ± 19.3 particles/g-dw) and in the gut of M. cephalus (230.7 ± 8.2 particles/g-dw). Fibers (FBs) were the predominant morphotype in both muscle tissue and gut, accounting for 92.7% and 97.1% of the detected particles, respectively. Polyethylene terephthalate predominated in muscle tissue (53.4%), whereas polypropylene predominated in the gut (68.7%). The calculated CF, PLI, PHI, and PERI values revealed marked differences in relative microplastic contamination and polymer-associated hazard among species, tissues, and sampling locations. These differences suggest that feeding behaviour, habitat use, and polymer composition may contribute to species- and tissue-specific microplastic exposure patterns. The detection of microplastics in muscle tissue, together with their variable polymer composition, highlights the ecological relevance of microplastic contamination in commercially important fish and the need for continued monitoring of microplastic occurrence and characteristics in the south-eastern Black Sea.

title: Modeling sorption dynamics and ecotoxicological risk of microplastics and polybrominated diphenyl ethers in Arctic and subarctic freshwater.
abstract: Microplastics can act as sinks and carriers for hydrophobic organic contaminants, including polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs), increasing their bioavailability and potential harm to Arctic and subarctic freshwater biota. However, the sorption dynamics, drivers of co-contamination, and combined toxicity of microplastics and PBDEs remain poorly understood. This study develops a Bayesian Network (BN) to assess PBDE sorption onto microplastics and evaluate the ecotoxicological risk of PBDE-enriched microplastics with an application to northern pike in Great Slave Lake, Canada. The model integrates the physiochemical properties of PBDEs and microplastics, seasonal fluctuations, and local environmental factors to forecast their co-contamination and exposure to pike. Additionally, it incorporates fish physiological parameters to predict the cumulative ecotoxicological risk to pike. The results show that PBDE concentrations, seasonal changes, and microplastic abundance are the strongest contributors to reduced cell viability and endocrine-related effects in northern pike. By linking contaminant interactions, environmental drivers, and biological outcomes, this research improves ecotoxicological risk assessment for hydrophobic pollutants associated with microplastics in Arctic and subarctic freshwater ecosystems. The findings can support policymakers in designing targeted monitoring and mitigation strategies to protect the Arctic and subarctic region.

title: Aged buoy-derived microplastics alter photosynthetic performance and metabolic regulation in Pyropia yezoensis without short-term growth inhibition.
abstract: Plastic aquaculture equipment can release microplastics into seaweed mariculture zones, yet the effects of these particles on cultivated macroalgae remain poorly understood. In this study, Pyropia yezoensis thalli were exposed to field-aged buoy-derived polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) microplastics at 0.1, 1, and 10 mg/L for 7 d. Relative growth rate was not significantly affected, whereas other sublethal endpoints showed polymer-specific changes. PVC exposure was associated with stronger lipid peroxidation, carbohydrate depletion at high concentration, and increasing integrated stress. PET exposure mainly induced protein accumulation and peroxidase-related antioxidant responses, with the highest integrated deviation occurring at the lowest concentration. Metabolomic profiling further supported these physiological patterns. PVC-related metabolic changes were mainly associated with antioxidant regulation, lipid metabolism, and pigment-related pathways, consistent with membrane oxidative damage and phycobiliprotein disturbance. PET-related changes were more closely linked to protein synthesis, transport regulation, and cofactor-dependent antioxidant processes. Overall, aged PVC and PET microplastics induced distinct sublethal responses in P. yezoensis, highlighting the need to consider polymer identity, aging status, and combined biomarker-metabolomic endpoints in ecological risk assessment of seaweed mariculture systems.

title: A validated Nile Red fluorescence method following KOH/H₂O₂ digestion for microplastic detection in marine molluscs.
abstract: Microplastic (MP) in marine ecosystems poses an increasing risk to the environment and human health. However standardized rapid methods for monitoring large numbers of samples are still lacking. This study validates a semi-automated Nile Red dye (NRD) fluorescence method combined with a two-step KOH/H₂O₂ digestion protocol for MP detection in marine molluscs. Twelve reference materials, including six synthetic polymer types (PE [two size fractions], PP, PA-66, PET, PMMA) and six natural materials (cotton, hemp, cellulose, wool, viscose, olive stone powder), were evaluated before and after digestion. Treatment resulted in 83.2 (± 4.8%) digestion of the natural reference, and reduced fluorescence intensity by 83.9 (± 14.9%). In comparison, the synthetic polymers lost only 13.0 ± 11.6% of their initial mass and 42.7 ± 18.4% of their fluorescence intensity, thus increasing the fluorescence discrimination ratio between synthetic and natural materials from 3-fold to 16.9-fold. The protocol retains the chemical integrity of the synthetic polymers (FTIR Hit Quality Index: 89.7-99.3%), which allows further reliable identification of the particles by FTIR. The protocol was applied to samples of Black Sea invertebrate organisms (M. galloprovincialis and R. venosa, 67 specimens) and achieved near-complete organic matter removal (>99.8%). The MP load was higher in M. galloprovincialis (median: 1.3 MPs g-1 WW; Q1-Q3: 0-3.2; n = 27) than in Rapana venosa (median: 0 MPs g-1 WW; Q1-Q3: 0-0.2; n = 40). This validated workflow provides a reproducible and cost-effective approach for large-scale MP monitoring in marine bioindicator species.

title: Advanced vulvar adenocarcinoma of mammary gland type: a case report.
abstract: Vulvar adenocarcinoma of mammary gland type (AMGT) is a rare, locally aggressive neoplasm of anogenital mammary-like glands that mimics the histologic and immunophenotypic features of breast carcinoma. Fewer than 60 cases have been described in the literature since the first documented case in 1936. The extreme rarity and resemblance to breast carcinoma complicate diagnosis and treatment. This report presents a case of AMGT in a 61-year-old woman who presented with a palpable, subcutaneous lesion of the lateral mons pubis and labia minora. Initial biopsy identified the lesion as metastatic carcinoma, but immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis and PET/CT indicated a vulvar adenocarcinoma with local nodal metastasis. Aggressive management with radical vulvectomy and bilateral inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy with thorough specimen evaluation by surgical pathology led to the final diagnosis of AMGT TNM stage pT1bpN2cM0 and vulvar FIGO Stage IIIC. IHC staining identified the tumor as ER, PR, and 3+ HER2 positive. Breast cancer treatment guidelines informed the ultimate systemic therapy regimen of docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab. Maintenance therapy with trastuzumab and anastrozole was utilized. The patient remained in remission from AMGT 24 months following completion of chemotherapy. While the diagnosis of AMGT poses a unique challenge, IHC staining and imaging to rule out metastatic carcinoma can support the ultimate diagnosis. The sustained remission in this case supports the extrapolation of treatment from vulvar and breast cancer guidelines. Additionally, this case suggests the utility of hormone receptor- and HER2-targeted therapies for systemic treatment.

title: An artificial intelligence-assisted PARP-1-targeted PET imaging agent [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-FZPF: From bench to clinic.
abstract: Considering that clinical data for 68Ga-labeled poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP)-targeted probes have not yet been reported and integrated artificial intelligence (AI) workflows for radiotracer development are still lacking, to support radiotracer development and clinical translation, we constructed an AI-assisted multi-stage prioritization workflow and then synthesized two 68Ga-labeled PARP-1-targeted probes, validating their performance through in vitro, in vivo, and clinical evaluations. An AI-guided multi-objective workflow (encoder-decoder recurrent neural network (RNN) generation, convolutional neural network (CNN) docking scoring, Synthetic Complexity Learned from a Reaction Corpus (SCScore)-based tractability triage, and deep neural network (DNN)) was used to prioritize a derivatization-ready Fuzuloparib analog (NH2-FZPF) and to guide chelator installation, yielding DOTA-FZPF and NOTA-FZPF precursors for subsequent 68Ga radiolabeling. Both [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-FZPF and [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-FZPF exhibited high radiochemical purity, stability, and PARP-1-targeted specificity. In tumor models, [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-FZPF displayed favorable tumor uptake and rapid background clearance, supporting further evaluation. Exploratory positron emission tomography (PET) assessments of Fuzuloparib target engagement show the specificity and functionality of [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-FZPF, supporting in vivo evaluation of PARP inhibitor target engagement and pharmacodynamics. This study recruited 4 cancer patients and performed positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) scans using [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-FZPF. Biopsy specimens showed that PET/CT-positive lesions corresponded to regions of high PARP-1 expression. This study demonstrates how an AI rational design workflow can support decision-making in radiotracer design while maintaining synthetic feasibility and translational potential. These preliminary findings support the clinical feasibility of [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-FZPF and suggest that it is promising for non-invasive assessment of PARP-1 expression and dynamic monitoring of in vivo target occupancy and pharmacodynamics.

title: A rare case of gallbladder torsion with incidental stage IIIB gallbladder adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Gallbladder torsion is rare and can mimic acute cholecystitis. We report an 83-year-old female who presented with abdominal pain, leukocytosis, and hyperbilirubinemia. Work-up showed a distended, thick-walled gallbladder with stones and suspected choledocholithiasis. Because of worsening pain and concern for impending perforation, she underwent urgent cholecystectomy, which revealed a freely mobile gallbladder consistent with torsion. Final pathology showed a 0.4 cm poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma with metastatic involvement of a cystic duct lymph node (stage IIIB). Postoperatively, she underwent endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography and removal of a retained common bile duct stone. Staging positron emission tomography/computed tomography demonstrated no residual or metastatic disease. Because the gallbladder was detached from the liver bed due to torsion, no further hepatic resection was performed, and systemic chemotherapy was recommended. This case illustrates both the diagnostic challenge of gallbladder torsion and a novel management consideration for incidentally discovered gallbladder cancer in the setting of a floating gallbladder.

title: Potential Role of BCL2 and BCL6 Overexpression in Circulating Tumor Cells as Molecular Biomarkers in DLBCL After R-CHOP Therapy.
mesh: Humans; Neoplastic Cells, Circulating; Lymphoma, Large B-Cell, Diffuse; Proto-Oncogene Proteins c-bcl-6; Doxorubicin; Biomarkers, Tumor; Female; Cyclophosphamide; Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols; Prednisone; Vincristine; Proto-Oncogene Proteins c-bcl-2; Male; Rituximab; Middle Aged; Aged; Adult; Antibodies, Monoclonal, Murine-Derived; Case-Control Studies; Treatment Outcome
abstract: UNLABELLED: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most prevalent non-Hodgkin lymphoma subtype. Although R-CHOP remains the standard first-line therapy, up to 30% of patients experience relapse or refractory disease. Currently, therapeutic monitoring relies on imaging, which is less sensitive than molecular techniques for detecting residual disease. AIM: To evaluate BCL2 and BCL6 oncogene expression in Circulating Tumor Cells (CTCs) as potential molecular biomarkers for clinical outcomes in DLBCL patients after R-CHOP therapy. METHODS: We analyzed BCL2 and BCL6 expression in CTCs from 42 patients post-R-CHOP using immunomagnetic enrichment of CD20+ cells followed by RT-qPCR. RESULTS: Patients exhibited significantly higher BCL2 (p = 0.003) and BCL6 (p = 0.001) expression than healthy controls. Overexpression of BCL2 and BCL6 was observed in 16.7% and 19% of patients, respectively, with 9.5% showing co-expression. Normal BCL6 expression correlated with complete response (p = 0.004), and BCL6 demonstrated high discriminative ability for disease activity (AUC = 0.791, p = 0.008). CONCLUSIONS: The presence of BCL2 and BCL6 in CTCs suggests that liquid biopsy serves as a robust, complementary tool to PET/CT for post-treatment monitoring. These findings support the utility of BCL6 as a biomarker for residual disease surveillance in DLBCL.

title: Ebullition-Enhanced Release of Microplastics from Aquatic Sediment to Overlying Water: An Overlooked Transport Pathway.
mesh: Microplastics; Geologic Sediments; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Polyvinyl Chloride
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) in aquatic systems are typically attributed to wastewater, runoff and atmospheric inputs, whereas the remobilization of sediment-associated MPs by benthic gas ebullition remains poorly understood. Here, we show that air-purged ebullition mobilized four common MPs, polyethylene (PE), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polylactic acid (PLA), from sediments into the overlying water, with release ratios of 8.9%-12.1% over 9 d. Suspended MP concentrations in the overlying water increased rapidly during the first 48 h, followed by slower release and eventual plateauing, with the decelerating release behavior empirically described by a power-law model. Theoretical calculations suggest that aggregation with suspended sediment can reduce the flotation velocities of MPs from 9.38-9.99 cm·s-1 to 8.64-9.95 cm·s-1. Combined experimental observations and theoretical analyses support a coupled flotation mechanism involving MPs attachment to rising bubbles, bubble-driven flow that counteracts gravitational settling, and transient pressure gradients. These processes could convert sediments from a long-term sink into a secondary source of MPs during ebullition. Overall, this study identifies benthic gas ebullition as an underappreciated pathway for MP remobilization and provides a mechanistic framework for understanding the fate and transport of sediment-associated MPs in aquatic environments.

title: Primary cardiac angiosarcoma: From pathogenesis to therapeutic strategies.
mesh: Humans; Hemangiosarcoma; Heart Neoplasms; Tumor Microenvironment; Male
abstract: Primary cardiac angiosarcoma (PCAS) is a rare yet highly aggressive malignancy arising from cardiac vascular endothelial cells. This tumor predominantly affects young to middle-aged males and carries a dismal prognosis, typically characterized by a median survival of less than one year. Owing to its nonspecific manifestations and rapid infiltrative growth, most patients present at an advanced or metastatic stage. Recent genomic and transcriptomic studies have revealed molecular drivers in PCAS, including recurrent mutations in POT1, KDR/VEGFR2, and PLCG1, loss of CDKN2A, and aberrant angiogenic cascade activation. In parallel, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment dominated by exhausted T cells and tumor-associated macrophages may collectively contribute to tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. Multimodal imaging, integrating echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance, computed tomography, and PET/CT, plays a central role in detection, tissue characterization, and systemic staging. Histopathology with immunohistochemistry remains the diagnostic gold standard. Current treatment strategies rely on multimodal approaches, including surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy, with emerging targeted therapies and immunotherapies under active investigation. Despite recent advances, clinical outcomes remain poor, highlighting the urgent need for improved mechanistic understanding and more effective personalized therapeutic strategies.

title: Performance of68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT for Diagnosing Tumor Thrombus and Predicting Response to Pembrolizumab and Axitinib in Patients with Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Pilot, Retrospective Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the performance of 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT for diagnosing tumor thrombus (TT) and predicting response to pembrolizumab and axitinib in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with TT. METHODS: We reviewed RCC patients who underwent contrast-enhanced CT, mpMRI, and 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT. Diagnostic performance for detecting TT was analyzed, with TT confirmed by experienced pathologists. We further analyzed clear cell RCC (ccRCC) patients with TT who received pembrolizumab and axitinib and evaluated imaging features for predicting therapeutic efficacy by using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling (1000 iterations). Model calibration was assessed with the Hosmer-Lemeshow test. RESULTS: A total of 166 RCC patients were initially included, of whom 56 had TT. 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT showed higher overall diagnostic performance for TT than contrast-enhanced CT and mpMRI, with incremental detection primarily observed for Mayo level 0-I TT. The sensitivity and specificity of PET/CT in diagnosing TT were 0.96 (95% CI 0.88-0.99) and 0.97 (95% CI 0.92-0.99), respectively. Then, 35 ccRCC patients with TT underwent an average of 5 cycles of pembrolizumab and axitinib, followed by surgery. Following neoadjuvant therapy, 21 patients exhibited a partial response, while 14 showed nonresponse. TT SUVmax demonstrated significant predictive value for response to neoadjuvant therapy, with an AUC of 0.80 (95% CI 0.63-0.92; bootstrap-corrected, 0.79). The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated adequate calibration (P > 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT may provide incremental value for detecting low-level TT and shows potential for predicting response to pembrolizumab plus axitinib in RCC. However, the clinical significance of detecting early TT remains uncertain.
